sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Action Cable integrates WebSockets into Rails, allowing the server to push updates to connected clients without polling. The architecture uses channels (analogous to controllers), streams (named pub/sub topics), and the Redis adapter for pub/sub across multiple Puma processes. Turbo Streams in Rails 7+ are built on top of Action Cable and represent the modern way to push real-time DOM updates. This page covers the full channel lifecycle (subscribed, unsubscribed, receive), Redis pub/sub vs polling vs SSE trade-offs, broadcasting from a Sidekiq job to connected clients, authentication in the connection handshake, and scaling Action Cable — the sticky-session requirement when multiple app servers are behind a load balancer and Redis is the pub/sub hub.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: cable-channels, redis-pub-sub, broadcasting, scaling-action-cable. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
